opening.text: And a history most of the world has never heard.

map.text: In ten nineteen, {Mahmud} of Ghazni marched on the {Chandelas}.
In twelve ninety-six, a raid on {Devagiri} paid for a murder, and a throne.
By thirteen eleven, the armies of Delhi had reached {Madurai}.
Out of the wreckage, new kingdoms rose.
And in seventeen forty-one, on a beach in Travancore, a Dutch force surrendered to an Indian king.

cards: {Vidyadhara} had the king of {Kannauj} killed, for running from {Mahmud} of Ghazni. Then he bought his own peace, with three hundred elephants, and a poem.
{Bhoja} was credited with books on poetry, temples, even machines. He lost his last war. He won his name.
{Simhana} made {Devagiri} the prize of the Deccan. Fifty years after his death, its gold bought a sultan his throne.
{Jatavarman} {Sundara} {Pandyan} took tribute from Lanka, killed a {Hoysala} king, and had himself weighed against gold.
Balban was sold as a slave. As sultan, he made the lords of Delhi kiss his feet. In public, he never laughed.
{Alauddin} {Khilji} fixed the price of grain, to pay the army that beat the Mongols. Then he massacred the Mongols who had fought for him.
{Bukka} {Raya} helped found {Vijayanagara}, and called himself Sultan among Hindu kings.
{Kapilendra} {Deva} seized a throne, and carried it from the {Ganga} to the {Kaveri}. His sons tore it apart.
{Lachit} {Borphukan} was gravely ill when the Mughal fleet came. He had himself carried onto a boat, and turned it back.
{Marthanda} {Varma} beat the Dutch, made their captured officer his general, then gave his kingdom to a god.
end: Blood and Thrones. A history, in ten lives.
